claims.text: The as-cast FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy has inherent microstructural heterogeneity.
Nanoindentation will reveal measurable local variations in hardness in as-cast FeNiCrMn.
Nanoindentation will reveal measurable local variations in elastic modulus in as-cast FeNiCrMn.
Local hardness and elastic-modulus variations correlate with microstructural heterogeneities.
Nanoindentation measurements can provide reliable insights into the mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn.
A controlled-load nanoindentation test using a standard indenter such as a Berkovich tip can be used to assess local mechanical properties.
A sufficiently dense indentation map can capture microstructural variations.
SEM and EBSD can be used to map microstructural features associated with indentation sites.
Relevant microstructural heterogeneities include local variations in grain size, phase distribution, and possible precipitation.
Interaction between indentation-induced plastic deformation and heterogeneous microstructure produces variations in measured hardness and elastic modulus.
Regions with refined grain structures will exhibit higher hardness and elastic modulus than coarser regions.
Regions with specific phase distributions will exhibit higher hardness and elastic modulus than less strengthened regions.
Conventional tensile or macro-hardness tests provide an overall averaged bulk response for comparison with local measurements.
Correlations between nanoindentation and bulk behavior may be limited to room-temperature, quasi-static loading.
